{{nihongo|'''Kuwabara Shrine'''|桑原神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

'''Kuwabara Shrine''' (くわばらじんじゃ) is a shrine along the {{ill|Kinugawa River|arz|نهر كينوچاوا|ceb|Kinu-gawa|fr|Kinu-gawa|it|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|ko|기누강|ru|Кину|zh|鬼怒川|qid=Q1042040}} in {{ill|Jōsō|ar|جوسو (إيباراكي)|azb|جوسو، ایباراکی|ce|Дзёсо|ceb|Mitsukaidō-shi|de|Jōsō|eo|Ĵoso|es|Jōsō (Ibaraki)|fa|جوسو، ایباراکی|fi|Jōsō|fr|Jōsō|gl|Jōsō|hy|Ձյոսո|id|Jōsō, Ibaraki|it|Jōsō|ja|常総市|ko|조소시|mg|Mitsukaidō|mzn|جوسو، ایباراکی|nl|Joso|pl|Jōsō|pt|Joso|ro|Jōsō|ru|Дзёсо|sv|Jōsō|tg|Ҷосо|tl|Jōsō|tr|Jōsō|tt|Дзёсо|tum|Jōsō|uk|Дзьосо|ur|جوسو|uz|Joso|vi|Jōsō, Ibaraki|war|Jōsō, Ibaraki|zh|常總市|zh_classical|常總市|zh_min_nan|Zyôsô-chhī|zh_yue|常總|qid=Q851149}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}. Its two principal deities are {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|Q11633375|qid=Q11633375}} and Ame-no-Kumahito. It is a shikinaisha of Okada District, {{ill|Shimōsa Province|Q1053695|qid=Q1053695}}, formerly ranked as a gosha. It was the sōsha (general tutelary shrine) of the former {{ill|Okada district|ja|岡田郡|pl|Powiat Okada|qid=Q11473723}} and {{ill|Toyoda district|Q11634160|qid=Q11634160|lt=Toyota District}}.

of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|Q1053695|qid=Q1053695}} and grandson of {{ill|Prince Shiki|Q11072254|qid=Q11072254}} (seventh son of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ar|الإمبراطور تينجي|azb|تنجی (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Tenji|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنجی|cs|Tendži|de|Tenji|es|Tenji Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنجی|fi|Tenji|fr|Tenji (empereur)|hak|Tenji Thiên-fòng|he|טנג'י|hu|Tendzsi japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenji|it|Tenji|ja|天智天皇|ka|ტენძი|ko|덴지 천황|nl|Tenji|pl|Tenji|pt|Tenji|ru|Император Тэндзи|sh|Car Tenji|simple|Emperor Tenji|sl|Cesar Tendži|sr|Car Tenji|sv|Tenji|th|จักรพรรดิเท็นจิ|tl|Emperador Tenji|tr|Tenji (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тендзі|uz|Imperator Tenji|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenji|wuu|天智天皇|yo|Emperor Tenji|zh|天智天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenzi Thian-hông|zh_yue|天智天皇|qid=Q314802}}), enshrined his ancestors "Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto" and "Ame-no-Kumahito-no-Mikoto" as guardian deities on a plateau called Motoyashiki on the west bank of the Kinugawa. Motoyashiki had a large settlement since ancient times and also had the 10-meter keyhole tumulus "Higashiyamazuka," now lost due to modern levee works.

During the Shotai era (898-901), Taira no Yoshimasa placed the Shimosa provincial office at Motoyashiki where this shrine stood and made it a political base. {{ill|Taira no Masakado|cs|Masakado Taira|de|Taira no Masakado|es|Taira no Masakado|et|Taira Masakado|fa|تایرا نو ماساکادو|fr|Taira no Masakado|ja|平将門|ko|다이라노 마사카도|nl|Taira no Masakado|pt|Taira no Masakado|ru|Тайра-но Масакадо|sh|Taira no Masakado|sr|Таира но Масакадо|th|ไทระ โนะ มาซากาโดะ|uk|Тайра но Масакадо|zh|平將門|zh_classical|平將門|qid=Q1207652}} also revered this shrine while using Motoyashiki as a base with his father {{ill|Taira no Yoshimasa|Q11483523|qid=Q11483523}}.<ref name="社頭石碑">Shrine-front stone monument "Origin of Kuwabara Shrine" (installed by Ishige Town Mayor, November 1988)</ref>

Because residents moved west from Motoyashiki due to flooding and other disasters, the shrine was also relocated to the present site in {{ill|1678|Q7634|qid=Q7634}} ({{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} 6). In {{ill|1712|Q6871|qid=Q6871}} ({{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shotoku}} 2), it was raised to Senior First Rank under the shrine name "Katori-sha." In {{ill|1719|Q6902|qid=Q6902}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 4), when rebuilding the main hall, a ridge tag from {{ill|1625|Q6826|qid=Q6826}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}} 2) reading "one shrine building established at Kuwabara Daimyojin, Kunou, Shimosa Province, Kanto, Japan" was discovered. In {{ill|1758|Q7639|qid=Q7639}} ({{ill|Hōreki|de|Hōreki|eo|Horeki-epoko|fa|هوره‌کی|fr|Ère Hōreki|it|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|ko|호레키|ru|Хорэки|simple|Hōreki|sr|Хореки|sv|Hōreki|tr|Hōreki|zh|寶曆 (日本)|qid=Q1194397}} 8), the temple-and-shrine magistrate recognized it as the Engishiki shrine "Kuwabara Shrine," and from then the name reverted to "Kuwabara Shrine."<ref name="社頭石碑"/>

In February {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 42), the following two shrines were merged into the main hall.<ref name="社頭掲示板">Shrine noticeboard "Kuwabara Daimyojin" (installed by {{ill|Ishige, Ibaraki|Q11584779|qid=Q11584779}} and Ishige Town Tourism and Products Association)</ref>
* Hie Shrine
* Satahiko Shrine

=== Precinct shrines ===
Enshrined at the back of the approach after passing the torii.
* Katori-sha

Enshrined on the right side facing the main shrine buildings.
* Osugi-sha
* Yonshagu

Enshrined on the left side facing the main shrine buildings. Among the stone shrines are two whose shrine names are not clearly marked.
* Koshin-sha
* Inari-sha, Hie-sha
* Tenjin-sha, Yasaka-sha, Hachiman-sha, Atago-sha
